description: §18.6.1 / §19.7.1 (S474) — the accepted way to handle every error of a failable `match` in one arm: `.Ok(v) :> "LOGGED IN", _ e :> "denied"`. `_ e` takes every error variant and never `.Ok`, so a wrong password yields "denied" and the right one "LOGGED IN". The form E-MATCH-ELSE-ABSORBS-ERROR's message offers.
provenance: ruling:user-voice-scrml.md S474 "⭐ RULED — `else` on a failable match; `scrml fix` S466 readings" item 1 — "Nothing becomes impossible to write, since every error can still be handled in one arm with `_ e`"
rationale: §18.6.1: in a `match` on a failable result, `_ <name>` matches every error variant not matched by an earlier arm and never `.Ok`. With an `.Ok` arm the match is exhaustive; no E-MATCH-ELSE-ABSORBS-ERROR (there is no plain `else`) and no E-TYPE-020.
